subject: science
angle: While the 10:1 ratio is widely cited, research shows the number of bacteria in the body is actually of the same order as the number of human cells.
title: The shared body

hooks.text: You are not ten times more human than microbe.
You ignore the trillions of lives living inside you.
A thumb resting on a wooden table.

reveal.headline: You are not ten times more human than microbe.
reveal.body: The number of bacteria in your body is of the same order as your own human cells.

explain.headline: The math of your body.
explain.body: In a 70 kg man, the count of bacteria is about 3.8·1013. The count of human cells is revised to 3.0·1013.

matters.headline: A shared existence.
matters.body: That may be why the line between yourself and your microbiome is less of a wall and more of a shared space.

example.headline: A quiet breath.
example.body: You sit in a chair and breathe. You feel like a single person, but you are a host for trillions of lives moving in sync with yours.

stat.label: estimated number of bacteria in a 70 kg man

claims.text: The number of bacteria in the body is of the same order as the number of human cells.
claims.quote: Our analysis also updates the widely-cited 10:1 ratio, showing that the number of bacteria in the body is actually of the same order as the number of human cells

claims.text: The number of bacteria in a 70 kg man is estimated to be 3.8·1013.
claims.quote: We estimate the total number of bacteria in the 70 kg "reference man" to be 3.8·1013.

claims.text: The total mass of bacteria in the body is about 0.2 kg.
claims.quote: and their total mass is about 0.2 kg.

claims.text: The number of human cells in the body is revised to 3.0·1013.
claims.quote: For human cells, we identify the dominant role of the hematopoietic lineage to the total count (≈90%) and revise past estimates to 3.0·1013 human cells.

claims.text: The total body counts are estimated at ≈36 trillion cells in the male, ≈28 trillion in the female, and ≈17 trillion in the child.
claims.quote: In total, we estimate total body counts of ≈36 trillion cells in the male, ≈28 trillion in the female, and ≈17 trillion in the child.

verdict: The evidence shows that bacterial cell counts are roughly comparable to human cell counts, contradicting the common 10:1 ratio.
caveat: The bacterial count is based on a 70 kg "reference man" and does not account for individual variation.
caption:
The boundary of your identity is thinner than you think.

Research shows that bacterial cell counts are roughly comparable to human cell counts, contradicting the common 10:1 ratio. This estimate is based on a 70 kg reference man and does not account for individual variation.

How does it feel to know you are a shared space?
